title: The Works of Aristotle — Classical Reference
content:
The Works of Aristotle — Classical Reference

I. Logic (The Organon)

1. Categories — classifies types of predication and being
2. On Interpretation (De Interpretatione) — language, propositions, truth and falsehood
3. Prior Analytics — formal syllogistic logic; the first systematic theory of deduction
4. Posterior Analytics — scientific demonstration, knowledge, axioms
5. Topics — dialectical reasoning, argumentation strategies
6. Sophistical Refutations — logical fallacies and how to expose them

II. Natural Philosophy (Physics)

7. Physics — causation, motion, change, place, time, the infinite
8. On the Heavens (De Caelo) — celestial bodies, the structure of the cosmos
9. On Generation and Corruption — coming-to-be and passing-away, elemental transformation
10. Meteorology — atmospheric and geological phenomena

III. Biology

11. History of Animals (Historia Animalium) — comparative anatomy and observation of animal life
12. Parts of Animals (De Partibus Animalium) — functional anatomy, why animals have the parts they do
13. Movement of Animals (De Motu Animalium) — how animals initiate locomotion
14. Progression of Animals (De Incessu Animalium) — mechanics of walking, swimming, flying
15. Generation of Animals (De Generatione Animalium) — reproduction, embryology, heredity

IV. Psychology

16. On the Soul (De Anima) — the nature of the soul, perception, intellect, imagination
17. Parva Naturalia (Short Works on Nature) — memory, dreams, sleep, sensation, longevity

V. Metaphysics

18. Metaphysics — being qua being, substance, form, potentiality, actuality, the Unmoved Mover

VI. Ethics

19. Nicomachean Ethics — virtue ethics, the good life (eudaimonia), moral character, friendship, justice
20. Eudemian Ethics — parallel ethical treatise, overlapping with the Nicomachean
21. Magna Moralia — summary of ethical doctrine (authorship debated)

VII. Politics

22. Politics — the state, citizenship, constitutions, justice, education, the best regime
23. Constitution of the Athenians (Athenaion Politeia) — history and structure of Athenian government

VIII. Rhetoric and Poetics

24. Rhetoric — persuasion, argumentation, emotions, style, three modes of proof (ethos, pathos, logos)
25. Poetics — tragedy, epic poetry, plot structure, catharsis, mimesis

Note: Many additional works attributed to Aristotle have been lost. Ancient catalogues list over 200 titles. What survives are primarily lecture notes and treatises from the Lyceum.
